name: Falcon 9 Block 5 (two-stage medium launcher)
source: Stage masses, thrust, Isp, burn times: SpaceX 'Falcon User's Guide' (2021) and spacex.com/vehicles/falcon-9 as summarised in the Wikipedia article 'Falcon 9 Block 5' / 'Falcon 9 Full Thrust' (figures quoted from memory, to verify against the user's guide). Capsule: Soyuz descent module figures as given in the Wikipedia article 'Soyuz (spacecraft)' (from memory, to verify). Flight profile for comparison: SpaceX launch webcast timelines (e.g. Crew missions: Max-Q ~T+1:02 to 1:12, MECO ~T+2:30, SECO-1 ~T+8:45, approximate).
licence: Numbers are facts from public documents (not copyrightable); no text, drawing or logo copied. Everything marked 'estimate' is our own.
visual: PLACEHOLDER: procedural cylinders and cones in stage colours, no livery, no logo

stages.name: Stage 1
stages.note: len includes the interstage (simplified); 162 s published burn includes throttling (full throttle here: ~147 s); gimbal 5 deg = estimate

stages.name: Stage 2
stages.note: ispSL never used (ignites high up); 397 s published burn; throttle range and gimbal = estimates

fairing.note: jettisoned when the free-molecular heating 1/2 rho v^3 drops below 1135 W/m2 (common fairing rule)

capsule.name: Capsule (Soyuz descent-module figures)
capsule.note: cd 1.3 hypersonic, ballistic (no lift), parachute areas, deploy altitudes and the deorbit perigee are estimates; soft-landing rockets not modelled

aero.note: ESTIMATE: axial drag vs Mach = a typical slender-launcher curve with the transonic peak near Mach 1.1-1.2, not measured data for this vehicle; normal force: Jorgensen, NASA TR R-474 (1977), potential part at 2/3 of the nose length, cross-flow part at the body centre

guidance.note: kick tuned here for a 200 km orbit (estimate): 11 to 15 deg reach orbit, 13 gives MECO near 75 km; 17 deg and more fail
